item.title: SCMP: White House confirms US-China-Russia trilateral on Apec sidelines
item.description: The White House on Friday confirmed an unprecedented meeting between leaders of the US, China and Russia has been scheduled to take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen next week. “President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the President of the United States, the President of the People’s Republic of China and the President of the Russian Federation,” said Olivia Wales, the White House assistant press...

item.title: SCMP: All US flights grounded due to communication issues: homeland security head
item.description: Air travel across the United States came to a halt on Friday afternoon after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered all flights grounded because of a communications breakdown at the regional centres that manage the country’s air traffic. Citing “extraordinary circumstances” and “reasons of safety”, the FAA said in a notice that the halt would stay in place until at least 11pm Eastern time on Friday. In a social media post, the agency described the problem as a temporary...

item.description: US lawmakers have been demanding answers about potential national security risks and White House oversight of advanced chip exports to China following revelations that former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was in a relationship with a businesswoman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. item.title: SCMP: Midterm losses could give Trump a quest to emerge from Apec summit as a winner
item.description: When G7 leaders gathered at the French resort of Evian-les-Bains in June, Donald Trump arrived late but wasted no time in grabbing the spotlight. With a cheeky declaration, “I am the boss”, the US president drew a ripple of awkward laughter from around the table. Months earlier, in his September 2025 address to the UN General Assembly, he told the gathering that “your countries are going to hell”. His lengthy speech blended boasts about his own record with sharp criticism of allies’ policies,...

item.title: SCMP: EU’s fixation on Chinese subsidies masks its own structural stagnation
item.description: The European Commission is moving to shield its industrial machinery and chemical sectors from Chinese imports, and is weighing a “kill switch” mechanism. Together with Washington, Brussels has settled into a familiar narrative: a record trade deficit with China is framed as proof of its “overcapacity” and attributed to state subsidies that allegedly tilt the global playing field. For European Union audiences frustrated by stagnant domestic manufacturing, this argument sounds intuitive. Held…

item.title: SCMP: Bessent blames US Commerce Department for not restricting Nvidia chip exports to China
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday blamed the Commerce Department, led by Howard Lutnick, for delaying the blacklisting of Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of diverting advanced AI chips to China, days before US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are expected to meet in Shenzhen. Bessent spoke a day after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive following reports that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at…

item.description: US President Donald Trump will press Southeast Asian economies to join Pax Silica, his campaign to China-proof AI and chip supply chains, when he attends the Asean summit in Manila next week. item.description: China and the United States have a shared interest in preventing artificial intelligence (AI) from being misused, but differing views over what constitutes a serious safety incident could complicate efforts to build a bilateral communication mechanism, according to analysts. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that Washington and Beijing should cooperate on AI risks while harbouring no illusions about their differences. item.title: SCMP: ‘10,000-tonne level talent’ biologist Zhao Yingming leaves Chicago for Hangzhou
item.description: In early November, a low-resolution photo of an internal meeting circulated on China’s social networks, accompanied by a caption with only one sentence: “It is said that he is a top-tier introduced talent at the 10,000-tonne level.” The main person in the photo is leading biologist Zhao Yingming, who was the Louis Block Professor in the Ben May Department for Cancer Research at the University of Chicago. item.title: SCMP: Algeria test-fires apparent Chinese YJ-12 supersonic missile in Mediterranean drill
item.description: Algeria’s military has released footage showing what appears to be the export variant of China’s YJ-12 supersonic anti-ship missile being test-fired along the country’s Mediterranean coast, offering a rare glimpse of an advanced Chinese weapon in service with one of Beijing’s African military customers. The weapon was launched from a mobile coastal-defence system near the western Algerian city of Oran on Tuesday, striking a target at sea during the country’s Mediterranean Falcon 2026 military...

item.title: SCMP: How a bad impression put a celebrated 2,000-year-old Han cliff inscription at risk
item.description: Reports that two Chinese nationals were convicted in Mongolia for making unauthorised impressions of a celebrated 2,000-year-old Han dynasty cliff inscription have ignited discussion and concern over protecting historic sites. The online uproar emerged this week as Chinese internet users and experts in Inner Mongolia noted that the landmark site had been subjected to illegal tampering since its rediscovery was made known nearly a decade ago. The case stems from an incident in November last…

item.title: SCMP: No research fund, no teaching job: late Chinese pianist’s note published by student
item.description: A Chinese pianist ordered to secure research funding to save his university job has died, while a note that he left exposing alleged malpractices at the institution was posthumously posted online by one of his students – with his family’s consent. The note was penned by Bai Baoguo. Born in 1972, Bai was an associate professor at the Yan’an University’s Luxun Academy of Fine Arts in Shaanxi province. He died on October 20. Two weeks later, on November 3, a six-page note circulated on the…

item.title: SCMP: Reporter’s notebook: shooting brings home grim reality in the US capital
item.description: We were weeks into a three-month assignment reporting from the SCMP bureau in Washington when we heard a shooting just around the corner from our apartment building. From our flat, we often hear trucks going past and loud noise from the ventilation system several storeys below. But as we got ready for work at 8am on Thursday we heard something unusual – “bang, bang, bang”. It was gunfire, and it sounded like it was right outside our apartment. Soon after, we heard fire alarms, police sirens…
